config.name: Citizenship
config.title: Canadian Citizenship
config.subtitle: Based on Discover Canada
config.disclaimer: Original practice questions based on the official study guide Discover Canada. Not affiliated with Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC).

questions.text: What document, added to the Constitution in 1982, sets out the rights and freedoms of Canadians?
choices: The Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms
questions.explanation: The Charter of Rights and Freedoms became part of the Constitution of Canada in 1982.

questions.text: Which of these is a fundamental freedom protected in Canada?
choices: Freedom of thought, belief, opinion and expression
questions.explanation: Fundamental freedoms include freedom of conscience and religion; thought, belief, opinion and expression; peaceful assembly; and association.

questions.text: Which document, signed in England in 1215, is the source of many of the freedoms Canadians enjoy?
choices: The Charter of Rights and Freedoms
questions.explanation: Magna Carta (the Great Charter of Freedoms) is part of the long tradition of rights and the rule of law that Canada inherited.

questions.text: What are the two official languages of Canada?
questions.explanation: English and French are Canada's official languages and have equal status in Parliament and federal institutions.

questions.text: Which of these is a responsibility of Canadian citizenship?
questions.explanation: Responsibilities include obeying the law, taking responsibility for oneself and one's family, serving on a jury, voting in elections, helping others in the community and protecting heritage and the environment.

questions.text: Which of these is a responsibility of Canadian citizenship?
choices: Serving on a jury when called
Moving to a new province every five years
questions.explanation: Serving on a jury is a legal obligation when called. Military service is voluntary in Canada.

questions.text: Which right do Canadian citizens have that permanent residents do not?
choices: The right to vote in elections and run for office
The right to a fair trial
questions.explanation: Only Canadian citizens can vote in federal and provincial elections and be candidates. Most other rights apply to everyone in Canada.

questions.text: What does "equality of women and men" mean in Canada?
choices: Men and women are equal under the law
questions.explanation: In Canada, men and women are equal under the law; violence and so-called "honour" crimes are severely punished.

questions.text: What is the term for the right of Canadians to enter and leave the country and live and work in any province?
questions.explanation: Mobility rights allow Canadians to live and work anywhere in Canada, enter and leave the country freely, and apply for a passport.

questions.text: What does the principle of "the rule of law" mean?
choices: The Prime Minister can change any law alone
Everyone, including governments and police, must obey the law
Only citizens must obey the law
questions.explanation: Under the rule of law no one is above the law, and government and police may not act arbitrarily.

questions.text: Who is Canada's Head of State?
questions.explanation: Canada is a constitutional monarchy. The Sovereign is Head of State; the Prime Minister is Head of Government.

questions.text: Who represents the Sovereign in Canada at the federal level?
questions.explanation: The Governor General represents the Sovereign in Canada; in each province a Lieutenant Governor does so.

questions.text: Who represents the Sovereign in each province?
questions.explanation: Each province has a Lieutenant Governor, appointed by the Governor General on the advice of the Prime Minister.

questions.text: What are the three parts of Parliament?
choices: The Prime Minister, the Cabinet and the courts
The provinces, the territories and the cities
The House of Commons, the Supreme Court and the police
The Sovereign, the Senate and the House of Commons
questions.explanation: Canada's Parliament has three parts: the Sovereign (represented by the Governor General), the Senate and the House of Commons.

questions.text: What are the three levels of government in Canada?
choices: Senate, House of Commons and Cabinet
Federal, provincial or territorial, and municipal (local)
questions.explanation: Canada has federal, provincial/territorial and municipal governments, each with different responsibilities.

questions.text: What is the head of a provincial government called?
questions.explanation: The Premier leads a provincial or territorial government, as the Prime Minister leads the federal government.

questions.text: Who is the Head of Government in Canada?
choices: The Speaker of the House of Commons
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister is the Head of Government; the Sovereign is Head of State.

questions.text: How are members of the Senate chosen?
choices: They are appointed by the Governor General on the advice of the Prime Minister
They are chosen by the provinces' premiers
They are elected by the people
questions.explanation: Senators are appointed and may serve until age 75.

questions.text: How are members of the House of Commons chosen?
choices: They are appointed by the Prime Minister
They are elected by the people in their electoral district (riding)
They are appointed by the Sovereign
They are chosen by the Senate
questions.explanation: Members of Parliament (MPs) are elected in federal elections, one for each electoral district.

questions.text: What is an electoral district also called?
questions.explanation: Canada is divided into electoral districts, also known as ridings; each elects one Member of Parliament.

questions.text: What must happen for a bill to become law in Canada?
choices: It must be approved in a national referendum
The Prime Minister must sign it alone
It must be approved by every province
It must be passed by both houses of Parliament and receive Royal Assent
questions.explanation: A bill passes the House of Commons and the Senate and becomes law when it receives Royal Assent from the Governor General.

questions.text: What is it called when the Governor General signs a bill passed by Parliament?
questions.explanation: Royal Assent is the final step that makes a bill law.

questions.text: What are the main parties in the House of Commons that are not in power called?
questions.explanation: Parties not in power are the opposition. The largest is the Official Opposition, which acts as a "government in waiting".

questions.text: Who chooses the Cabinet ministers?
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister selects the Cabinet ministers, who run federal departments.

questions.text: What is the minimum age to vote in a federal election?
questions.explanation: Canadian citizens 18 years of age or older can vote in federal elections.

questions.text: Is voting in Canada a secret ballot?
choices: Yes, no one can watch you vote or force you to tell how you voted
No, votes are counted by name
questions.explanation: Canada uses a secret ballot. You may discuss your vote, but no one can require you to reveal it.

questions.text: What is the role of the courts in Canada?
choices: To settle disputes and decide on guilt or innocence according to the law
questions.explanation: The judiciary is independent; courts settle disputes and the Supreme Court of Canada is the highest court.

questions.text: What is the highest court in Canada?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court of Canada is the final court of appeal.

questions.text: Which national police force enforces federal laws throughout Canada?
questions.explanation: The RCMP enforces federal laws everywhere in Canada and provides policing in provinces and territories that do not have their own force.

questions.text: Which provinces have their own provincial police forces?
questions.explanation: Ontario (OPP) and Quebec (Sûreté du Québec) have provincial police; the RCMP polices most other provinces.

questions.text: What is a constitutional monarchy?
choices: A system run by the military
A system with no Head of State
A system in which the Sovereign is Head of State but power is exercised according to a constitution
A system in which the King makes all laws
questions.explanation: Canada is a constitutional monarchy, a parliamentary democracy and a federal state.

questions.text: What is the Speech from the Throne?
choices: A speech by the Supreme Court
The speech that opens a new session of Parliament and outlines the government's plans
questions.explanation: The Speech from the Throne is read by the Governor General at the opening of a session of Parliament.

questions.text: Who were the first peoples to live in what is now Canada?
questions.explanation: Indigenous peoples lived in Canada for thousands of years before the arrival of European explorers.

questions.text: What are the three main groups of Indigenous peoples in Canada?
questions.explanation: The Constitution recognizes three groups of Aboriginal peoples: First Nations, Inuit and Métis.

questions.text: Who are the Métis?
choices: A distinct people of mixed Indigenous and European ancestry
questions.explanation: The Métis are a distinct people of mixed Indigenous and French or British ancestry; many live in the Prairie provinces.

questions.text: Where do most Inuit live?
questions.explanation: The Inuit live mainly in the Arctic regions; their name means "the people" in Inuktitut.

questions.text: Who founded Quebec City in 1608?
questions.explanation: Samuel de Champlain founded the first permanent French settlement at Quebec City in 1608.

questions.text: Which explorer claimed the land for the King of France in the 1530s?
questions.explanation: Jacques Cartier made three voyages across the Atlantic between 1534 and 1542 and claimed the land for France.

questions.text: Which company was granted rights to the fur trade around Hudson Bay in 1670?
questions.explanation: The Hudson's Bay Company received exclusive trading rights over the lands draining into Hudson Bay in 1670.

questions.text: Which battle in 1759 marked the end of France's empire in America?
choices: The Battle of the Plains of Abraham
questions.explanation: The British defeated the French at the Plains of Abraham at Quebec City in 1759.

questions.text: Who were the Acadians?
choices: Descendants of French colonists in the Maritimes
Settlers from the United States after 1776
questions.explanation: The Acadians, descendants of French colonists who settled in the Maritimes from 1604, were deported by the British in the "Great Upheaval" (1755–1763).

questions.text: Who were the United Empire Loyalists?
choices: People who stayed loyal to the Crown and moved to Canada after the American Revolution
questions.explanation: More than 40,000 Loyalists settled in Nova Scotia and Quebec after the American Revolution.

questions.text: In which war did Canada help defend against an American invasion in 1812–1814?
questions.explanation: In the War of 1812 the United States invaded Canada and was pushed back; this helped ensure Canada would remain independent of the U.S.

questions.text: Which British general is remembered for his role in defending Upper Canada in the War of 1812?
questions.explanation: Sir Isaac Brock captured Detroit and was killed at the Battle of Queenston Heights in 1812.

questions.text: Who was Laura Secord?
choices: A woman who walked many miles to warn British troops of an American attack in 1813
The founder of the Hudson's Bay Company
questions.explanation: Laura Secord's warning helped the British and Indigenous forces win the Battle of Beaver Dams.

questions.text: In what year did Confederation take place?
questions.explanation: The Dominion of Canada was created on July 1, 1867.

questions.text: Which four provinces were the first to join Confederation?
choices: Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick
Ontario, Manitoba, Alberta and British Columbia
Quebec, Newfoundland, Prince Edward Island and Nova Scotia
questions.explanation: Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick formed the Dominion of Canada in 1867.

questions.text: Who was Canada's first Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: Sir John A. Macdonald, a Father of Confederation, became Canada's first Prime Minister.

questions.text: What are the "Fathers of Confederation"?
choices: The judges of the first Supreme Court
The leaders who worked together to create Canada in 1867
questions.explanation: Representatives of the colonies worked together from 1864 to 1867 to establish the new country.

questions.text: What was the name of the Act that created Canada in 1867?
choices: The Charter of Rights and Freedoms
The British North America Act (Constitution Act, 1867)
questions.explanation: The British North America Act, now called the Constitution Act, 1867, created the Dominion of Canada.

questions.text: Which railway, completed in 1885, connected Canada from sea to sea?
questions.explanation: The completion of the Canadian Pacific Railway in 1885 linked British Columbia with the rest of Canada.

questions.text: What was the Underground Railroad?
choices: A smuggling route during the War of 1812
A railway built under the Rocky Mountains
A network that helped slaves escape from the United States to Canada
questions.explanation: Thousands of slaves escaped to Canada through the Underground Railroad, a network of anti-slavery people.

questions.text: Who led the Métis resistance in the 1869 and 1885 uprisings in Western Canada?
questions.explanation: Louis Riel led two Métis uprisings; he was executed for high treason in 1885 and is seen today by many as a defender of Métis rights.

questions.text: Which province was the last to join Canada, in 1949?
questions.explanation: Newfoundland and Labrador joined Canada in 1949.

questions.text: Which territory was created in 1999?
questions.explanation: Nunavut, meaning "our land" in Inuktitut, was created in 1999 from the eastern part of the Northwest Territories.

questions.text: Which First World War battle in April 1917 became a symbol of Canada's national pride?
choices: The Battle of the Plains of Abraham
questions.explanation: Canadians captured Vimy Ridge in 1917; it is often seen as a symbol of Canada's coming of age as a nation.

questions.text: On D-Day, June 6, 1944, which beach did Canadian troops capture?
questions.explanation: Canadian troops landed on and captured Juno Beach in Normandy as part of the Allied invasion.

questions.text: In which year did most Canadian women get the right to vote in federal elections?
questions.explanation: Most Canadian women won the right to vote in federal elections in 1918. Manitoba was the first province to grant women the vote, in 1916.

questions.text: Who was the first woman elected to the House of Commons?
questions.explanation: Agnes Macphail, a farmer and teacher, was elected to Parliament in 1921.

questions.text: Who was Terry Fox?
choices: A hockey player who invented the game
A young athlete who began the "Marathon of Hope" across Canada to raise money for cancer research
questions.explanation: After losing a leg to cancer, Terry Fox began his cross-country run in 1980; the annual Terry Fox Run continues today.

questions.text: What are residential schools?
choices: Government-funded boarding schools where Indigenous children were taken from their families and suffered abuse
questions.explanation: Residential schools sought to erase Indigenous languages and cultures. In 2008 Ottawa formally apologized to former students.

questions.text: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.explanation: Ottawa, chosen by Queen Victoria in 1857, is the capital of Canada.

questions.text: How many provinces and territories does Canada have?
questions.explanation: Canada has ten provinces and three territories (Yukon, Northwest Territories and Nunavut).

questions.text: What is the national anthem of Canada?
questions.explanation: "O Canada" was proclaimed the national anthem in 1980. "God Save the King" is the royal anthem.

questions.text: When did the red-and-white maple leaf flag become Canada's national flag?
questions.explanation: The maple leaf flag was raised for the first time in 1965.

questions.text: What is the motto of Canada, "A mari usque ad mare", in English?
questions.explanation: "A mari usque ad mare" means "from sea to sea".

questions.text: When is Canada Day celebrated?
questions.explanation: Canada Day, July 1, celebrates the anniversary of Confederation in 1867.

questions.text: What is commemorated on Remembrance Day, November 11?
choices: The sacrifice of veterans and soldiers who served and died in wars
questions.explanation: On Remembrance Day Canadians wear the red poppy and observe a moment of silence at 11 a.m.

questions.text: Which flower do Canadians wear to remember the war dead on Remembrance Day?
questions.explanation: The red poppy, inspired by the poem "In Flanders Fields", is worn in the weeks before Remembrance Day.

questions.text: Who wrote the poem "In Flanders Fields"?
questions.explanation: John McCrae, a Canadian medical officer, wrote "In Flanders Fields" during the First World War.

questions.text: What is Canada's most popular spectator sport and official winter sport?
questions.explanation: Hockey is Canada's most popular spectator sport and its national winter sport; lacrosse is the official summer sport.

questions.text: What is Canada's official summer sport?
questions.explanation: Lacrosse, an ancient sport first played by Indigenous peoples, is Canada's official summer sport.

questions.text: Which animal is an official symbol of Canada?
questions.explanation: The beaver was adopted as a symbol by the Hudson's Bay Company and is an official emblem of Canada.

questions.text: Which leaf has been a Canadian symbol since the 1700s and appears on the national flag?
questions.explanation: The maple leaf is Canada's best-known symbol and appears on the flag.

questions.text: The Parliament Buildings are in which city?
questions.explanation: The Parliament Buildings stand on Parliament Hill in Ottawa.

questions.text: Which ocean lies to the west of Canada?
questions.explanation: Canada borders the Pacific to the west, the Atlantic to the east and the Arctic to the north.

questions.text: Which ocean lies to the north of Canada?
questions.explanation: The Arctic Ocean lies to the north of Canada.

questions.text: Which country shares the longest border with Canada?
questions.explanation: The Canada–United States border is the longest undefended international border in the world.

questions.text: Which are the Prairie provinces?
choices: Nova Scotia, New Brunswick and Prince Edward Island
questions.explanation: Manitoba, Saskatchewan and Alberta are known as the Prairie provinces.

questions.text: Which are the Maritime provinces?
choices: New Brunswick, Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island
questions.explanation: The Maritime provinces are New Brunswick, Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island.

questions.text: What is the smallest province by area?
questions.explanation: Prince Edward Island is the smallest province; it is known for its red soil and potatoes.

questions.text: Which is Canada's largest city by population?
questions.explanation: Toronto, the capital of Ontario, is Canada's largest city.

questions.text: Which province has the largest French-speaking population?
questions.explanation: Most Francophones live in Quebec. New Brunswick is the only officially bilingual province.

questions.text: Which is the only officially bilingual province?
questions.explanation: New Brunswick is the only province that is officially bilingual (English and French).

questions.text: Which province is Canada's major producer of oil and gas?
questions.explanation: Alberta has the largest oil and gas reserves in Canada, including the oil sands.

questions.text: Which mountains lie in British Columbia and Alberta?
questions.explanation: The Rocky Mountains run through British Columbia and Alberta.

questions.text: What are Canada's three main types of industry?
choices: Service, manufacturing and natural resources industries
questions.explanation: The service industry employs most Canadians; manufacturing and natural resources are also major industries.

questions.text: Which is Canada's largest trading partner?
questions.explanation: Canada has close economic ties with the United States, its largest trading partner.

questions.text: What is the capital of British Columbia?
questions.explanation: Victoria is the capital of British Columbia; Vancouver is its largest city.

questions.text: What is the capital of Alberta?
questions.explanation: Edmonton is the capital of Alberta; Calgary is the province's largest city.

questions.text: What is the capital of Nunavut?
questions.explanation: Iqaluit is the capital of Nunavut. Yellowknife is the capital of the Northwest Territories and Whitehorse of Yukon.
